title: Minimizing Array After Replacing Pairs With Their Product
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, you can repeatedly combine adjacent elements x and y into a single element x * y if x * y <= k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, you can repeatedly combine adjacent elements x and y into a single element x * y if x * y <= k. The goal is to find the smallest possible length of the array after performing any number of such operations.
constraints: nums is nonempty and contains nonnegative integers; k is positive.
Adjacent values may merge into their product only when that product is at most k.
Return the minimum possible remaining array length.
reference_solution:
def minimum_product_merge_length(nums,k):
    if 0 in nums:return 1
    groups=1;product=nums[0]
    for value in nums[1:]:
        if product*value<=k:product*=value
        else:groups+=1;product=value
    return groups

hints: With positive values, extending the current merge group only increases its product; a zero can absorb the whole array.
Greedily make each left-to-right product group as long as allowed, starting a new group only when necessary.
Return one immediately for any zero; otherwise multiply while product*next<=k and count forced boundaries.
A failed product cannot be repaired by ending the current group later, while accepting a feasible next value never reduces future grouping options, so earliest maximal groups minimize count.
